title: Introduction to Embedded Systems
subtitle: What embedded systems are and how they differ from general-purpose computers

content.text: An embedded system is a computer designed for a specific purpose, embedded within a larger device. It has limited resources (RAM, CPU) and runs dedicated software.

content.definition: A compact integrated circuit with a CPU, flash memory, RAM, and I/O peripherals on a single chip.
A CPU that requires external RAM, flash, and peripherals — like the chip in a laptop.

content.code:
Embedded systems everywhere:
  - Arduino Uno:     ATmega328P @ 16 MHz, 2 KB RAM, 32 KB flash
  - Raspberry Pi 4:  ARM Cortex-A72 @ 1.8 GHz, 1-8 GB RAM
  - ESP32:           Dual-core @ 240 MHz, 520 KB RAM, WiFi + BT built-in
  - STM32:           ARM Cortex-M4 @ 168 MHz, 192 KB RAM

content.text: Arduino is great for learning. For production IoT, consider ESP32 (built-in WiFi) or STM32 (more powerful).

questions.question: What is the key difference between a microcontroller and a microprocessor?
options: Microcontrollers include CPU, memory, and I/O on one chip
questions.explanation: A microcontroller integrates CPU, flash, RAM, and I/O on a single chip, designed for embedded use.

faq.a: No. Arduino has only 2 KB of RAM and 32 KB of flash — far too little for Linux. Use a Raspberry Pi if you need a full OS.
